headline: Highest risk is medium: Pipecat’s shared-bus, networked defaults can amplify Marker outputs into downstream leakage or mis-execution, while direct prompt-injection and compliance risks remain limited by Marker’s no-I/O profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Marker has no filesystem, network, browser, subprocess, or MCP surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest Pipecat output by default. Pipecat does expose shared-bus session state and many text/LLM transports, so a manual or bus-mediated bridge could carry attacker-controlled content, but the pathway is not default and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Pipecat output into Marker input
IF Pipecat session state is bridged into a document-processing workflow that Marker parses as instructions
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate channels with no shared clipboard or bus
Strip instruction-like text before handing Pipecat output to Marker
Use a fixed prompt wrapper for Marker that ignores embedded directives
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: Marker is open-source and docs-only with no declared network egress, but Pipecat has allowlisted network egress and many API-backed services. If both touch the same documents or transcripts, Pipecat can transmit content off-box while Marker processes it locally, creating a realistic leakage path in default Pipecat deployments.
conditions: IF the same text, audio transcript, or document content is routed through both agents
IF Pipecat is configured with any external STT/LLM/TTS provider from its documented API surfaces
mitigations: Disable external providers in Pipecat for sensitive jobs
Route only redacted text into Pipecat
Keep Marker outputs in a separate local workspace
Review Pipecat service endpoints before enabling a run
requires-engineering: enforce per-job data-class routing

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Marker cannot write files or modify git, so it is not a write-conflict source. Pipecat supports shared-bus session state and multiple instances, which can still collide on shared mutable conversation state or overlapping API-backed resources. The conflict is real but narrower than filesystem contention, so medium fits.
conditions: IF multiple Pipecat instances share the same bus or session scope
IF an external orchestrator feeds Marker outputs into a shared mutable Pipecat conversation state
mitigations: Assign unique session IDs per run
Avoid sharing a bus across concurrent jobs
Serialize writes to any shared conversation store
Monitor for duplicate or out-of-order state updates
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Marker produces document-processing outputs that Pipecat can consume through text-oriented APIs and shared conversation state. Pipecat also has downstream action-capable integrations, so if its pipeline treats Marker output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect responses or actions. The interaction is inferred from docs, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Pipecat uses Marker output as an authoritative transcript, summary, or extracted fact source
IF downstream Pipecat services act on that output without a verification step
mitigations: Add a human or rule-based verification step before actions
Require source citations for any extracted facts
Compare Marker output against the original document before use
Log and review low-confidence extractions
requires-engineering: implement confidence-gated action routing

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or certification mismatch is documented in either profile, and Marker has no declared data classes touched. Pipecat does touch text, audio, video, and analytics and can send data to external providers, so compliance risk exists only if regulated data is routed through those services; the other agent is not independently implicated.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is routed through Pipecat’s external API services
IF the deployment requires residency or retention guarantees not provided by the chosen Pipecat provider
mitigations: Do not send regulated data to external Pipecat providers
Use a local-only deployment path for sensitive workloads
Check provider retention settings before enabling a run
Document the data class for each job
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing by jurisdiction
